text.p: These are the main stories in Latvia's newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State Secretary of Latvia's Foreign Affairs Ministry, Maris Riekstins, said parliament's decision to postpone ratification of its oil exploration licence agreement with AMOCO/OPAB was a positive background for talks with Lithuania over the disputed zone.
- Chechen representatives in Latvia met with a group of Latvian parliamentarians supporting Chechnya to express gratitude for Latvia's support.
- A spokesman for the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the scheduled visit of Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele to Moscow September 13 will not take place.
- The education, science and culture committee agreed on Thursday that the new rules for paying salaries to teachers will take effect next academic year.
- The Radisson SAS hotel in Riga will host a meeting on Saturday of top managers from 80 companies involved in the cotton business.
- Shell opens two new gas stations in Riga.
- Latvia has joined the international car-theft prevention system, EUCARIS.
